question.worked_solution:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2} & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=18{x}^{2} & \,⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int 18{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=6{x}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 18{x}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}(6{x}^{3})-\int (6{x}^{3})(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =6{x}^{3}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-12\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={x}^{2} & \,⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})-\int (\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{3}-\frac{1}{3}\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{3}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{9}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 18{x}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =6{x}^{3}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-12\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =6{x}^{3}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-12(\frac{{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{3}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{9}+D) \\  & =6{x}^{3}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-4{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\frac{4{x}^{3}}{3}-12D \\  & ={x}^{3}(6{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\frac{4}{3})+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-12D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}18{x}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\text{d}x & ={[{x}^{3}(6{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\frac{4}{3})]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =[{e}^{3}(6{(\operatorname{ln}⁡e)}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡e+\frac{4}{3})]-[{1}^{3}(6{(\operatorname{ln}⁡1)}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡1+\frac{4}{3})] \\  & =[{e}^{3}(6-4+\frac{4}{3})]-\frac{4}{3} \\  & =\frac{10{e}^{3}-4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
